Anyone have experience doing payment plans for a guitar (like at Sam Ash, GC)?

I can't say that I have any experience whatsoever with any of these sort of payment plans. I'd assume it would be like any other line of credit. Be sure you're not getting bent over on interest rates, and make sure there aren't any insane put-it-in-your butt clauses anywhere in the contract, etc.

What makes it so tempting is whenever I go to sam ash I see advertisements for '0% interest' on the payment plan. I can't think of anything other than a sharp penalty for missing payments that could be in the contracts that would make deals like this undesirable.
I'd just read the terms very carefully. Personally, the thought of buying anything on credit makes my butt clench up.

I bought my first Gibson this way. I opened the credit card. They were offering 0% financing for the first 12 months. So I jumped on it, and paid it off within 6 months.

I had been playing for 7 years at this point, and I had an Epiphone Les Paul with a repaired headstock break. I felt I owed it to myself to finally get my first really nice guitar.

If you do it, I would definitely look for the 0% financing offers they do, because that card had like a 20% interest rate. I only did it because I knew I could afford it.

I got my gibson from guitar center like this. Honestly they're the most civil card company I've ever worked with. Missed a payment because their automated system went down and I didn't know it. They called me and asked if I knew, comped the fees and did the payment right there. Never changed the bill date on me like Synchrony likes to do with all their cards.

If you want a nice "in-between" option, Sweetwater does a 3 month no interest payment plan that doesn't feel as invasive or complex and is over pretty quickly. I'm also a big fan of their selection, their pictures and their service.

It won't be $24 a month for a new Les Paul but for something sub-$1,000 it's a cool option.
